as_told.title: Admiral Byrd's statement to the Chilean press

related.note: Both are about Byrd and Operation Highjump. Dolan reads Byrd's statement as not being about flying saucers, while the story claims the fleet met laser-shooting discs.

plain: The story concerns Operation Highjump, a large American expedition to Antarctica in 1946 and 1947, and a statement made afterwards by its leader, Richard Byrd. A researcher named Jason Jorjani tells Michels that when Byrd reached a port in Chile, he told the Chilean press that the US needed to prepare for a third world war "in which aircraft could cross from pole to pole at tremendous speeds." Jorjani credits this to Chilean press clippings and tells it as a hint that Byrd met unknown aircraft in Antarctica. A researcher named Richard Dolan disagrees about what it means. He says he read Byrd's whole statement and that "if you really read the whole thing I don't think he's really talking about flying saucers." So both men agree Byrd made a statement, but they read it differently: as a warning about strange craft, or as something more ordinary.
